findings.heading: Import data / データをインポート
findings.proposition: The translation instructs the reader to import the linelist with rio::import(); the code chunk immediately below (jp lines 43-51) calls appliedepidata::get_data(name = "linelist_cleaned_rds"), which is what the English text names.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader follows an import route that does not appear in any chunk on the page, and does not learn the appliedepidata::get_data() call that the shown code actually uses, so copying the visible chunk contradicts the instructions they just read.

findings.heading: Import data / データをインポート
findings.proposition: The translation tells the reader to click a raw GitHub URL (github.com/appliedepi/epirhandbook/raw/main/data/case_linelists/linelist_cleaned.rds) to download the cleaned linelist as an .rds file; the English has no download link and no .rds download step.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader is sent to a manual download workflow the English edition abandoned, and depends on an external raw-file URL that the handbook no longer maintains, instead of the package data accessor.

findings.heading: Import data / データをインポート
findings.proposition: The translation adds that the rio package handles many file types such as .xlsx, .csv and .rds, and cross-references the import/export chapter; the English segment contains neither claim nor that cross-reference.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader spends attention on rio, which this page never uses, and treats the import/export chapter as the prerequisite for this page's data step.

findings.heading: Flow diagrams / フローチャート
findings.proposition: Step 6 of the basic structure closes the instructions with `}")` in the English; the translation writes `}"`, omitting the closing parenthesis of the grViz() call.
findings.reader_consequence: A reader who follows the numbered structure literally writes an unclosed grViz( call and gets a syntax error, with no other step in the list telling them the parenthesis is still open.

findings.heading: Syntax / 構文
findings.proposition: The English says the curly-bracket subgroup on one side of an edge is a shorthand; the translation says it is optional / can be omitted (省略可能です), which is a statement about the edge, not about the notation being an abbreviation.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader understands the grouped edge itself as an optional element rather than as a compact way of writing several edges, and so may drop the braces and lose the edges to every node in the group.

findings.heading: Syntax / 構文
findings.proposition: The edge attribute `minlen` is documented as minimum length in the English and as 長さの最長値 (maximum value of length) in the translation, which is the opposite bound.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader sets minlen expecting to cap the edge length and instead forces edges to be at least that long, producing a diagram stretched in the direction opposite to what they intended.

findings.heading: Complex examples / 複雑な例
findings.proposition: In the displayed sub-graph cluster example the translation writes `Primary [label = '第一\n施設]` with no closing single quote, while the executed chunk beside it (jp line 396) and the English display block both close the string.
findings.reader_consequence: A reader who copies the displayed code, which is the only version shown as text to copy, gets an unterminated DOT string and a grViz() failure that does not point at the missing quote.

findings.heading: Plotting from dataset / データセットからプロット
findings.proposition: The English states that the code ensures the values are class Character before combining them; the translation instructs the reader to check that hospital and age_cat are character type before creating the name column, although the chunk beside it performs the coercion itself with as.character().
findings.reader_consequence: The reader believes a manual class check is required of them and may add or expect a preparatory step, while missing that as.character() in the chunk is what guarantees the type.
